tests.name: test_uses_its_arguments
tests.description: It gets every input from make and asks prop about it, the two functions it is given, not functions of the script.

tests.name: test_finds_failure
tests.description: With the inputs 1, 2, 3 and so on, and a property that fails only for 3, it gives 3, after making exactly 3 inputs.
tests.message: check gives 1 after making the inputs [1], where it should give 3, the first input for which the property is False, after making just [1, 2, 3].

tests.name: test_first_failure
tests.description: When the property fails for 3 and for 5, it gives 3, the first.
tests.message: With the property failing for 3 and 5, check gives 1, not 3.

tests.name: test_none_when_all_pass
tests.description: When the property holds for every input, it gives None, after making exactly trials inputs.
tests.message: check gives 1, not None, though the property held for every input.

tests.name: test_trials_limit
tests.description: It makes no more than trials inputs: a failure at the 20th input is not reached in 10 trials.
tests.message: check gives 1, not None, though the property held for all 10 inputs it should make.

tests.name: test_gives_the_input
tests.description: It gives the input itself, the very list that make gave, not True or False.
tests.message: check gives [0], not [2], the input for which the property is False.

tests.name: test_prop_once
tests.description: It asks the property about each input once, in order.
tests.message: The property was asked about [1], not [1, 2, 3, 4].

tests.name: test_zero_trials
tests.description: With 0 trials it makes no input, and gives None.

tests.name: test_reports_the_failure
tests.description: Given the tests a, b and c, of which only b fails, it gives ["b"].
tests.message: run_tests stopped with the AssertionError of a failing test, so the tests after it never ran.

tests.name: test_goes_on
tests.description: After a test fails, the tests after it still run: when a fails, b and c are called too.
tests.message: run_tests stopped with the AssertionError of a failing test, so the tests after it never ran.

tests.name: test_all_fail
tests.description: When every test fails, it gives every name, in order.
tests.message: run_tests stopped with the AssertionError of a failing test, so the tests after it never ran.

tests.name: test_all_pass
tests.description: When every test passes, it gives an empty list.

tests.name: test_each_once
tests.description: It calls every test exactly once, in the order of the dictionary.
tests.message: run_tests stopped with the AssertionError of a failing test, so the tests after it never ran.

tests.name: test_no_tests
tests.description: An empty suite gives an empty list.

tests.name: test_passes_right
tests.description: Your test passes a right median.

tests.name: test_uses_its_argument
tests.description: Your test calls the median it is given, and no other.

tests.name: test_upper_middle
tests.description: It fails wrong median A.
tests.message: Your test_median passes wrong median A, which gives the upper of the two middle values for an even number of values. Which list would tell it from a right median?

tests.name: test_unsorted
tests.description: It fails wrong median B.
tests.message: Your test_median passes wrong median B, which takes the middle of the list as it is, without sorting it. Which list would tell it from a right median?

tests.name: test_whole_mean
tests.description: It fails wrong median C.
tests.message: Your test_median passes wrong median C, which rounds the mean of the two middle values down to a whole number. Which list would tell it from a right median?

tests.name: test_no_repeats
tests.description: It fails wrong median D.
tests.message: Your test_median passes wrong median D, which keeps only one of each repeated value. Which list would tell it from a right median?

tests.name: test_in_place
tests.description: It fails wrong median E.
tests.message: Your test_median passes wrong median E, which puts the list it is given in order, changing the caller's list. How could a test see that?

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: For [1, 2, 1, 1], with fails true when a list has a repeat, it gives [1, 1].

tests.name: test_explore
tests.description: For the Explore phase's [7, 3, 9, 3, 5], it gives [3, 3].

tests.name: test_still_fails
tests.description: What it gives still fails, for several lists with a repeat.

tests.name: test_pair
tests.description: For a list with a repeat, it ends with just two equal numbers, since every other item can be taken out.
tests.message: shrink(fails, [3, 4, 3, 3, 4]) gives [4, 3, 4], but every item except two equal numbers can be taken out, and the list still fails.

tests.name: test_other_property
tests.description: With fails true when a list holds a number above 5, [1, 2, 9, 3] shrinks to [9].
tests.message: With fails true when a list holds a number above 5, shrink(fails, [1, 2, 9, 3]) gives [2, 9], not [9].

tests.name: test_leaves_the_list
tests.description: It leaves the caller's list as it was.
